anchors: The language skills add their own tools on top of this one; the method is shared.
decision: Performance is covered by three skills: this generic one, coding-python-performance-review and coding-rust-performance-review; this one routes by language.
reopen_if: Claude Code loads skill bodies partially, or a language skill shrinks to a few lines.
why: Each description triggers on its own language, and an invoked SKILL.md loads whole, so a Rust task must not load the 610-line Python body.

decision: One renamed performance skill with references/python.md and references/rust.md.
reopen_if: Skill triggering stops depending on the description text.
why: Its description would list every language and trigger less precisely, and every task would load the router first.

anchors: Two halves: how to measure so that a number means what you think it means
decision: This skill holds both the measurement method and a language-neutral review checklist.
reopen_if: The checklist grows language-specific entries a language skill should own.
why: A language with no skill of its own needs a list of what to look for, and the method must live in one place instead of being copied into each language skill.

decision: General words (commit, message, change, language, measuring, comparing, reviewing) among the first fourteen keyword tokens of the description.

evidence.text: skill-router match() over four reported prompts and 1998 typed prompts from local transcripts: the general-word head nominated the skill on 'fix the typo in the commit message' and 'which language should the docs be in, reviewing them now'; the performance-word head nominates neither and nominates 'the bash script loops over hosts and is slow'.

reopen_if: The skill router stops deriving keywords from the head of the description, or MIN_HITS changes.
why: The router derives this skill's keywords from the first fourteen distinct description tokens and nominates on two hits, so general words nominated it for prompts about commit messages and doc language while a slow bash loop got no match. Performance-specific words (slow, profile, benchmark, noise, latency, throughput, queries, unbounded, memory, loops) fix both.

anchors: rebuild the before arm yourself from
decision: With only a relative speedup claim and no recorded before figure, rebuild the before arm from the commit or diff, run both arms on the same recorded input, then apply the reproduce-before check.

evidence.text: Queue entry 60 (2026-11-07 review). GREEN opus and haiku rebuilt the before arm from the PR's parent before judging.

reopen_if: Step 2 is restructured so a measured baseline is always required up front.
why: Step 2 presumed a recorded before number; a review of a claimed 20 percent speedup had to improvise.
